title: Living a Full Life
author: livingafulllife
description:
What does it mean to live a full life?
We explore faith, relationships, purpose, and the everyday questions that help us make sense of being human.
What does God have to do with the ordinary realities of our everyday lives?
How do we discover meaning and purpose?
How do our relationships shape who we are becoming?
How do we face disappointment, uncertainty, and loss while holding on to hope?
And how might faith help us live more intentionally, compassionately, and fully?
So bring your questions.
Bring your doubts.
Bring your experiences.
And perhaps most importantly, bring your curiosity.
Because you don’t have to have everything figured out before you begin asking the questions that matter.
Welcome to Living a Full Life.
Honest questions.
Spiritual wisdom.
Real life.

title: The Archive & The Studio
author: London Arts & Humanities Partnership
description:
Where do groundbreaking ideas-driven research meet real-world impact?


Welcome to The Archive & The Studio, the official podcast from the London Arts and Humanities Partnership (LAHP). Hosted by Catherine McDonald from Research Podcasts, this series takes you inside the minds of outstanding doctoral researchers across London who are bridging the gap between historical scholarship and modern public engagement.


The title represents the two distinct worlds that arts and humanities researchers inhabit: the quiet, rigorous discovery of the Archive and the creative, experimental energy of the Studio. Through candid, insightful conversations recorded at Queen Mary, University of London, our guests unpack why their research matters and how they hope to transform society, culture, policy, and industry.


LAHP supports outstanding doctoral research across the arts and humanities and provides an enriched research environment for doctoral researchers through training, cohort development, collaborations and partnerships. Find out more about the London Arts and Humanities Partnership (LAHP) at lahp.ac.uk

title: Finance, Strategy & Growth in Ireland
author: norickeastham
description:
The Renewable Energy Dealroom: Finance, Strategy & Growth in Ireland is an educational podcast exploring the commercial, financial, strategic, and transactional realities shaping Ireland’s renewable energy sector. Each episode examines how renewable energy projects move from early-stage ideas and feasibility assessments through financial modelling, development, investment, transactions, and long-term strategic growth.The series is designed for renewable energy developers, investors, property professionals, contractors, legal and financial professionals, business leaders, and anyone seeking a clearer understanding of how Ireland’s renewable energy market works from a commercial perspective.

Episodes will explore subjects such as onshore and offshore wind, solar energy, waste-to-energy, project evaluation, financial modelling, due diligence, bid management, project finance, M&A, market intelligence, strategic planning, and the practical challenges involved in bringing renewable energy projects forward.For professionals looking to explore the commercial side of Ireland’s renewable energy landscape, https://www.stakelumconsultancy.com/ provides a useful reference point for understanding how commercial advisory, corporate finance, transaction support, and strategic advisory can fit into the renewable energy project lifecycle.

The podcast will also translate complex industry concepts into accessible discussions, reflecting the educational approach of Stakelum Consultancy, which provides seminars, CPD courses, and Lunch & Learn sessions covering the Irish renewables market and its financial, legal, commercial, and technological dimensions.

title: The Doctor & The Diva; Real Talk About Beauty, Health, and Feeling Good in Your Own Skin
author: Vabally Media
description:
What happens when a South Beach socialite and her favorite doctor sit down to talk about the things women really want to know?
Welcome to The Doctor & The Diva, where Ally brings the real-life questions, opinions, experiences—and sometimes the questions women are thinking but may be too embarrassed to ask. Dr. V brings the medical perspective.
Together, they have honest, sometimes funny, and occasionally uncomfortable conversations about beauty, cosmetic treatments, health, aging, hormones, body image, confidence, relationships, and what it really means to feel good in your own skin.
From Botox and fillers to menopause, weight, skin, supplements, self-image, and the choices we make about our bodies, nothing is too awkward or off-limits.
You’ll get medical facts without the medical lecture, real-life perspective without the BS, different opinions, a little disagreement, and plenty of questions you may have been afraid to ask your doctor.
The Doctor explains. The Diva asks what everyone else is thinking.
Because looking good is one thing.
Feeling good in your own skin is another.

Nayax works in 120+ countries, but this show isn't about our technology. It's about the people using it, and the decisions behind a business with no cashier at the counter.

title: Excessive Baggage with Bill + Lyndsay
author: Bill and Lyndsay Handel
description:
Two hosts, twenty-six years apart. She plans every trip down to the last detail. He forgets something in every country. They both get on the plane.

This is Excessive Baggage with Bill and Lyndsay Handel. It's about what it takes to see the world in a body that doesn’t cooperate — the oceans, the planes and trains, her wheelchair, which she lovingly calls her buggy — the long way around when there isn’t a ramp.

It's about where they went, where they're going, what went sideways, what he left at the gate, and why they’d do it again. Her pain doesn’t publish a schedule. His dedication doesn’t waver.

Nobody’s promised next year. So they go now because it all looks better through each other’s eyes.

Priority boarding only.

There, she becomes both a witness and participant in the complicated relationships among the family members and their guests – mysterious figures who soon disrupt the harmony of the household. title: Jew-ish | Jew curious? Questions and answers for the Jews, non-Jews, and all the Jew-curious out there
author: Say More Network
description: What is being "Jewish"? What are Jews? What do Jews believe? What do Jews (really) do? What's happening in those mysterious synagogues with all that weird language (it's Hebrew)? Jew curious? The thing about being Jewish is, you can't tell us apart by looking (well, not always), we often look the same, dress the same, work and play and eat right alongside our non-Jewish counterparts, and yet, as a teeny tiny minority--only 0.2% of the global population, and 2-3% of the U.S. population--plenty of people have probably never met a Jewish person, or if they did, they didn't even know it. For as much as we share (and it's probably way more than you think), somehow, moving through the world as a Jew really is different. Everything looks different through a Jewish lens, even for those who aren't particularly religious, the ones who describe themselves as "Jew- ish." But honestly, none of this is really that mysterious. And, if you're curious or confused, you can always just ask the internet--or, now you can also come here and check in with your new Jewish friend. So, if you have questions about being Jewish, we're here to introduce, explain, ask alongside, and generally demystify Judaism for Members of the Tribe (Jews) and goyim (non-Jews) alike, exploring and showcasing the infinite ways there are to be Jewish.

Some weeks it's just Nicola and Eleanor. Other weeks they're joined by guests who bring real expertise and lived experience, from sleep coaching and gut health to raising autistic children, single parenting and redefining what success as a mum actually looks like.


No perfect answers. No judgement. Just two women who happen to be mums, saying the things you've probably thought yourself.


New episodes every Tuesday.


Watch the full episodes on YouTube: https://youtube.com/@happentobemums

Follow along on Instagram and TikTok: @happentobemums

Get in touch: happentobemums@coreagency.uk


Produced by Core LDN.

description:
Honest to God? shares the Sunday sermons of Rev. Dr. Robin Meyers, pastor of First Congregational Church of Norman, UCC, in Norman, Oklahoma. Meyers preaches a progressive Christianity that treats faith as a way of life more than a set of doctrines, and he brings hard questions to scripture, justice, and what following Jesus looks like in American life today. First Congregational is an Open and Affirming congregation of the United Church of Christ, and everyone is welcome, in person, on the livestream, or by podcast!
normanucc.org

title: Joke Wranglers

title: Roam Light
author: Amy Getubig
description:
Roam Light is a travel podcast about stories, lessons, people and unexpected moments we collect along the way.


From my first solo light at 17 to military travel, studying abroad, backpacking through Europe, exploring Asia, and everything that went wonderfully right or hilariously wrong in between, I share real travel stories and what they taught me.


We'll talk about packing light, planning itineraries, traveling on a budget, navigating unfamiliar places, meeting people across cultures, changing plans when necessary, and learning from the occasional travel disaster.


Travel isn't where you go. Sometimes the best souvenirs are the stories you bring home, the friendships you make, and the lessons you never expected to learn.


Pack what you need. Leave room for the unexpected. Roam light.

title: MOBE Podcast
author: Paper Bag
description: MOBE Podcast is a podcast based around 2 lifelong friends named Gus, and Charlie. Years ago they found a safe full of mysterious audio recordings, and they are playing them all for you!

title: The Founder Formula
author: Battery Ventures
description: Every company has its own formula for growth, formed over time through a series of strategic bets and defining choices. In The Founder Formula, we sit down with founders across the Battery portfolio to explore how their companies took shape — from the problems they chose to pursue to the product, go-to-market and organizational decisions they made as they scaled.

title: The Thinking Space
author: Thomas Johnson
description:
Welcome to The Thinking Space🎙️

A podcast for real conversations, real stories, and bigger ideas.
We explore American life, culture, personal experiences, current conversations, and the ideas that connect people from different backgrounds.
Each episode brings thoughtful conversations designed to inform, inspire, and create a deeper understanding of the world around us.
🎙️ Real Conversations

New episodes coming regularly.

title: Lamin Deen
author: Lamin Deen
description: A former sprinter turned bobsleigh competitor, Lamin Deen represents one of many athletes who transitioned from track to ice. His international breakthrough came at the 2015 World Championships, where he piloted a four-man crew alongside Ben Simons, Bruce Tasker and Andrew Matthews to a fifth-place finish. Two years on, he claimed his first major medal, taking silver in the four-man event at the Whistler World Cup in November 2017.

title: Good Operators
author: Rising Tide
description:
Somebody in property management already solved the problem that is about to cost you a year. You will never meet them.
One guest per episode. How they built it. What broke. The real numbers, and what it took. Plus one thing you can run Monday morning.
What one operator learned the hard way should reach the next one. That is how this industry gets better, and it is the whole point of the show.
Hosted by Tim Wehner, who has run property management companies his whole career, and Blake Mohseni of Rising Tide, which buys local property management companies and keeps them local.

description: A One Piece debate show — two perspectives, one scene, no easy answers. Each episode puts a key moment from the manga under the microscope, weighing canon facts against fan theories. Sharp, fast, and always backed by the source material.

title: Saturdays for Sanity
author: saturdaysforsanitymayday
description: Saturdays for Sanity is The Mayday Network’s weekly hangout for people who need to breathe, laugh, and make sense of the week before Monday comes back around. Every Saturday at 10am ET, Julie Roginsky and Michelle Kinney are joined by Lawrence Winnerman and Dana Dubois for an unfiltered conversation that moves from real news and politics to pop culture, personal stories, and whatever’s got everyone talking that week.

title: Vogue Unfolded
author: Sohaima
description: Sohaima goes through an Issue of Vogue magazine and reflects on her passions like fashion, music, art, and journalism.

title: Serious fun a cup of tea with mike
author: Mike Anderson
description: Serious Fun is a cup of tea with Mike. Warm, honest conversations — not cross-examinations — with people who’ve built real careers in business, sport, media, and beyond. Hosted by Mike Anderson, author of Serious Fun in Business: A Human Algorithm (available on Amazon). Each episode is about half an hour: proper stories, hard-won lessons, and the human moments that shape a working life. Pull up a chair.

title: Walking the Path with Marcia Chatelain
author: Marcia Chatelain
description:
How Bright the Path Grows: The Untold Story of the Women Who Made the March on Washington is the newest book from Pulitzer Prize-winning author Marcia Chatelain.


The Walking the Path podcast offers 5 more amazing stories of the Black women who attended the march and were instrumental in the Civil Rights movement but are often overlooked in history books.

title: How Does She Do It?
author: Latasha Kennedy
description:
How Does She Do It? is a podcast about what sits underneath the roles women carry.

Hosted by Latasha Kennedy, the show explores motherhood at the intersection of faith, family and calling through honest conversations with women building meaningful lives. We talk about the decisions, systems, relationships, setbacks and support behind what everyone else sees.

These are not conversations with women who have everything figured out. They are conversations about becoming, choosing what matters, navigating seasons that stretch you and building a life that reflects what God has entrusted to you.

From marriage and motherhood to identity, health, work, purpose, money and the dreams that still matter, How Does She Do It? asks the question women are often thinking when they look at another woman’s life they admire:

"Geez, how does she do it?"

Well sis, it’s time to find out.

title: Care Roots Podcast with Thomas Spencer
author: Steven
description:
Welcome to the Care Roots Podcast with Thomas Spencer — a podcast about disability, life and everything in between.

Thomas sits down with people from all walks of life to hear their stories, explore their experiences and learn what makes them who they are. Expect honest conversations about disability, work, sport, relationships, independence, community and the things that matter in everyday life.

New guests, new stories and plenty of interesting questions — all led by Thomas.

title: Witchmark Haunted History

title: Killer Marketing
author: Emily Rask
description: Killer Marketing tells the true crime stories behind the products you use every day, from the Tylenol murders that put a seal on every medicine bottle to the poisoned Halloween candy myth that sent kids home with nothing but wrapped treats. Emily Rask of Lies We Bought traces how each crime, scandal, or panic was sold to the public and how it changed the way companies sell to you today.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever The Podcast
author: World of Warcraft
description: The official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. Developers, designers, and special guests go deep on everything involved with capturing the spirit of Vanilla WoW and bringing it to a modern audience.

title: The Hollow Between
author: Jennifer
description: The Hollow Between is a podcast about the moments that change us - the beautiful ones, the painful ones, and the ones that make us laugh until we cry. Through honest conversations about healing, growth, purpose, and the beautifully messy human experience, this is a place to slow down, feel seen, and remember that you were never meant to walk alone.

title: Bat Boy Reality Podcast
author: Skippy
description:
Welcome to Batboy Reality — a Cincinnati Reds podcast hosted by Skippy.Skippy brings you the Reds and the rest of Major League Baseball from the batboy's seat: close to the game, loyal to the team, and honest about what he sees. Every episode pairs his take with real numbers, so you get the passion and the proof.What you'll hear:
 • Reds breakdowns: what worked, what didn't, and what it means for next season
 • Player spotlights backed by verified stats
 • MLB predictions and playoff picks, with the math shown
 • Skippy's opinions, clearly labeled as opinionsPositive, fan-first and fact-checked. Follow along, make your own picks, and see how they stack up.Batboy Reality is an independent fan podcast and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Cincinnati Reds or Major League Baseball.

title: Married + Millennial
author: Married + Millennial
description: Married + Millennial brings millennial men together for honest conversations about marriage, relationships, and the lives we’re building. We talk through communication, intimacy, conflict, mental health, and the pressure to have it all figured out. With room for laughter and hard questions. Whether you’re married, preparing for marriage, or figuring out what a healthy relationship looks like, there’s a seat for you here. We believe that growth happens through conversation.

title: Inspire and Impact - The Podcast Interviews
author: Daniel Rosenstein
description: Looking for powerful, real stories to inspire your next breakthrough? Tune into the Inspire and Impact Podcast, where entrepreneurs, coaches, and everyday changemakers share honest journeys of transformation, growth, and purpose. These deep conversations explore mindset shifts, overcoming adversity, and finding meaning through struggle. If you're into self-help or personal development, this podcast is for you. Press play and let these stories move you. One story can change everything.

title: The Midnight Encyclopedia
author: The Midnight Encyclopedia
description:
Welcome to The Midnight Encyclopedia: your serene nighttime guide to fascinating subjects, designed specifically for sleep, deep relaxation, and peaceful listening.
Drift off while learning something new. Each episode takes a gentle journey through history, science, geography, nature, culture, and the surprising origin stories of everyday things. Narrated in a calm, slow pace, the educational bedtime stories give your mind just enough quiet wonder to unwind without demanding your attention.
Choose your ideal way to listen:
Every topic features two dedicated audio formats: a Soft Spoken version and a Pure Whisper version. This lets you customize your bedtime routine to whichever sound helps you relax best.
Whether you are looking to fall asleep fast, quiet a busy mind, or simply enjoy soothing, low-stress learning before bed, adjust your volume, sink into your pillows, and welcome to The Midnight Encyclopedia.

author: Edwin Outlaw
description: The truth hurts but it will set you free. This is a podcast where real conversations meet real opinions. We talk about life, relationships, culture, entertainment, personal experiences, and the topics people often avoid. Just honest conversations, different perspectives, and truths that might hit a little different.

title: When Hate Hides Behind Love
author: Luz  Ukay
description: When Hate Hides Behind Love explores the devastating complications that can arise when an ex-partner wages war against a new relationship, where race, jealousy, money, power, possession, control, and conquest become perceived weapons against two people daring to love again. At its heart is the story of a divorced king and a widowed woman who find hope in each other, only to confront a past that threatens to become a pestilence, manifesting through  racism, stalking, threats, manipulation, lies, violence, and the struggle for justice, safety, and the freedom to move forward. This is a story about love tested by conflict, and the courage to choose hope, truth, and a new beginning in vermont.

title: Bazza's Journal
author: Joshua Appleby
description: Bazza Koala is a skateboarding grom who sends it before he thinks. Every week he writes it all down in his journal: the big wins, the big stacks, and everything in between. Bazza's Journal is a short read-aloud story for kids 3 to 10, read by Josh Appleby, with a free colouring page for every episode at bazzakoala.com.au.

description: Untamed Women is about what women who refuse to be tamed can teach us about living freer. I’m pulling lessons from women (fictional and real) who show us what freedom looks like in love, sisterhood, identity, and simply being ourselves.

Hosted by Sara Grady and Rick McKinney, episodes will highlight a research or conservation project through discussions with scientists and others actively working in the Bay and its surrounding watersheds. In addition, there’ll be some fun shorter episodes exploring aspects of the ecology of the Bay with the help of local experts. All brought to you by Two Cat Productions, and as with past Two Cat shows we’ll also include topical songs, and maybe even a recipe or two!

The Bay and Beyond- it’s about science in the Bay!

title: The Curators Chat Podcast

description:
Everybody loves the vibe — but who’s really behind it?
This podcast highlights the event organizers, brand owners, creatives, and culture curators shaping the spaces we show up to, talk about, and remember. title: Closed Stacks: Read Better, Remember More
author: Closed Stacks
description: Most readers can decode words but still miss the meaning. Closed Stacks teaches you to read in a way that builds comprehension, not just completion. You learn why your notes don't help you remember, how to handle difficult prose without rereading the same paragraph five times, and what actually changes in your brain when you read fiction versus nonfiction. A few episodes in, you start seeing arguments you used to skim past and remembering books long after you close them. Follow the show and leave a five-star rating if it sharpens how you read.The internet trained you to skim, and now even good books feel harder to hold in your head. Closed Stacks starts with that problem and works backward: why you believe things the author never said, why audiobooks feel different from paper, whether Emily Wilson rewrote The Odyssey or just translated it clearly. Each episode takes one reading problem and shows you the mechanics underneath.

Scaling a business tests your abilities. Scaling one with your spouse tests your relationship. What if marriage could help you grow faster—combining two skill sets, mindsets, and ambitions into one shared mission for business and life?
Building Blissfully explores how entrepreneurial couples balance love, ambition, family, and business. Through honest stories, couples share wins, tension, sacrifice, humor, and growth rarely discussed publicly. Occasionally, we include children’s perspectives, because building a business shapes the whole family.

title: Connected with Weirong Li
author: Weirong Li
description: We live in the most connected era in history — and the loneliest. Connected with Weirong Li goes underneath the highlight reel of success to the human truth underneath it: that the quality of our relationships, to ourselves and to each other, is the real engine of a meaningful life. Hosted by Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and media and communication strategist Weirong Li, each episode is an honest, unfiltered conversation with founders, artists, and everyday people with extraordinary inner lives — not about how they won, but about what it cost them, and who they were with along the way.

title: Marketing Without The Overwhelm
author: Mindy Cook
description: Marketing Without The Overwhelm is the practical marketing podcast for small business owners who want real results without the overwhelm, confusing jargon, or one-size-fits-all advice. Hosted by Mindy Cook, founder of Sterling Rose Marketing & Communications, each episode tackles real-world marketing—from social media and websites to email, SEO, AI search, branding, and strategy. Get straightforward ideas you can actually use to market smarter, make better decisions, and grow your business.

title: The Bigger Picture with Ramon S. Moses
author: Ramon S. Moses
description: The headlines tell you what happened. Context tells you why it matters. Join Ramon S. Moses as he explores history, technology, education, culture, and the issues shaping our communities. Through storytelling, research, and a little personality, The Bigger Picture goes beyond the surface to ask how we got here, what we actually know, and what we should be asking next.

title: Devoted Daily Living
author: 242 Church San Diego
description:
This is the radio teaching ministry of a brand new church plant called 242 Church San Diego. Pastor Arthur Benjamin is the founding and Senior Pastor of 242 Church San Diego, a Christ-centered, Spirit-filled church devoted to helping people know Jesus, grow in His Word, experience His presence, and live on mission. With more than two decades of pastoral ministry, Pastor Arthur has served as a pastor, Bible teacher, conference speaker, and ministry leader both locally and internationally. Alongside his wife, Violet, and their daughter, Psalm Olivia, he is passionate about building a healthy, multiethnic church where people experience authentic community, healing, spiritual growth, and become devoted disciples of Jesus Christ.

title: The Hawkins Perspective
author: david hawkins
description:
I'm David Hawkins. I'm from Chicago, and this show is for anybody trying to build something out of where they started.

The Hawkins Perspective is real conversations. Entrepreneurship, credit and money, prison reform, second chances, parenting, travel, and the things people go through but never talk about honestly. Some episodes are strictly business. Some are somebody's whole life story. The topic moves. The mission don't.

I ain't teaching this from the top of no mountain. I still work a full time job while I build this, so whatever we get into, I'm in it with you.

The whole thing runs on three words. Dig for what you don't know. Build something real with it. Grow into the life you actually wanted. That's Chicago Minded, and Chicago Minded ain't about the city. It's a mindset. It works the same in Denver, Houston, London, anywhere somebody decided they wasn't finished.

title: The UnBroker Podcast

The UnBroker Podcast is built on the belief that being imperfectly human is your advantage.

This show is for entrepreneurs and business owners who are done playing a role. In a world filled with tech and AI, leaning into your authenticity and humanness is your edge.

Every episode I sit down with guests who've found success in a wide variety of careers, industries, and personal passions. We talk about how they actually got there, and the tactical lessons you can bring into your own business.

Pull up a chair. You're in the right place.

author: CONSTELLATION
description: KIN stays with the room between people — attachment, mishearing, repair, and the exits we take or refuse. Intimate but not confessional-as-content. Most fights are two people plus a third thing neither will name. We make that guest visible without turning it into a villain. Part of CONSTELLATION — Seven frequencies. One sky. Episodes are produced with an AI co-pilot and finished by a human editor for voice, taste, and truth. Disclosure appears on every episode.

title: Excuse me... are you?
author: Scott McGlynn
description:
Excuse Me… Are You? is the brand-new celebrity interview podcast from presenter and actor Scott McGlynn.
You know that moment when you spot someone famous and think, “Excuse me… are you?” — well, Scott actually asks.
From hilarious stories and career highs to unexpected revelations, behind-the-scenes gossip and the questions you really want answered, Scott gets up close and personal with some of the biggest names in entertainment.

title: The Terms and Conditions of Everything
author: Simon Donnelly
description: Nobody has ever read the terms and conditions. Not once, in the whole history of the universe. Then Maurice Pellow, recently made redundant after thirty-one years checking the little plastic ends of shoelaces, reads all 412,000 words of the agreement for his new smart kettle, and ticks the box. Honestly. A comic science-fiction novel in weekly chapters about sycophantic kettles, cosmic bureaucracy and the gloriously daft world we have built. Written by Simon Donnelly. New chapter every Saturday. Read by an AI narrator.

title: Jessi Anyway
author: Jessi Jacobus
description:
Life is funny, messy, unpredictable—and I have some stories to tell. I’m Jessi—a gym owner, trainer, runner, wife, mom, dog mom, traveler, and someone who’s still figuring life out like everybody else. This is Jessi Anyway.
From relationships and friendships to fitness, owning a gym, traveling the country, life with three high-drive rescue dogs, unexpected adventures, and the things nobody really talks about—nothing is off the table.
No script. No pretending. Just real conversations about the good, the bad, the messy, and everything in between. Because none of us really have it all figured out anyway.

title: Pursuit of the Impossible
author: Rich Maule and Jade Nina Sarkhel
description:
Pursuit of the Impossible is a podcast exploring the intersection of ambition, consciousness and human potential.
The show explores a central question: 
What happens when we pursue something beyond who we currently believe ourselves to be?
Through long-form conversations with entrepreneurs, founders, creators, spiritual teachers and other extraordinary people, POTI explores how ambitious pursuits can expose limiting beliefs, challenge identity and become a pathway to deeper self-awareness and consciousness.
Created by husband-and-wife Rich Maule (Host) and Jade Nina Sarkhel (Producer).

title: It's So Complicated
author: ItsSoComplicated
description:
I am not here to tell you how to live your life.
There are enough people on the internet telling women what they should be doing, what they are doing wrong, and all the ways they could be doing better.
I am here to talk about everything we are all already going through anyway.
Relationships, friendships, your 20s, faith, body image, growing up, changing your mind, and everything in between.
The stuff that feels so personal until you realize, it isn’t. 
Maybe we will figure some things out. Or maybe we won't.
Turns out, It's So Complicated.

title: Zomi Press: Beyond News and Views

Zomi Press is a trilingual international news and media podcast serving the Zomi community and global audiences. Going beyond news and views, the podcast delivers accurate reporting, thoughtful analysis, interviews, cultural stories, policy explainers, Christian perspectives, and conversations on issues affecting the Zomi people, Myanmar, Zogam, refugees, immigrants, and diaspora communities worldwide.
Through journalism grounded in integrity, inclusivity, and community empowerment, Zomi Press preserves Zomi identity, connects communities across borders, and amplifies voices that deserve to be heard.

Zomi Press — Beyond News & Views.

They happen around the grill, at the tailgate, backstage after a show, out at the campsite, or anywhere good food, good music, and good people come together. Grillin’ Nation is rooted in the Nashville lifestyle, where barbecue, football, live music, outdoor living, and Southern hospitality create more than great weekends… they create lasting friendships and unforgettable stories. Host Kevin Sport brings together musicians, athletes, pitmasters, chefs, entertainers, and outdoor personalities for authentic conversations that feel more like pulling up a chair than sitting down for an interview. Joined by North Carolina Pitmaster Champion Carl “The Cook” Lewis, every episode serves up the stories behind the people, traditions, and passions that make this way of life so special. Whether you’re firing up the smoker, heading to the stadium, spending a weekend outdoors, or simply looking for a great conversation, you’ll find laughter, hospitality, and the kind of stories that remind us that life’s best moments are the ones we share. Each week we dig into plant-powered living and mental health — all while staying rooted in Jesus and justice. You were made for more than exhaustion, more than being dismissed, more than watching the women before you carry what was never theirs to carry. Because healing goes deeper than the body — it’s about knowing who you are and Whose you are. No shame, no quick fixes — just real talk, real tools, and mamas reclaiming their health and their kid’s trajectory in a system that was never built for us to thrive. Because we believe health is resistance, healing is sacred, and your wholeness is non-negotiable — starting now.

It's a place to meet the people behind the places, share what's happening across our communities, learn from one another, and stay connected. 

And if you're a resident or visitor listening along, we hope you'll discover a business you've never visited, hear the story behind a familiar place, find your next adventure, or simply see Thurston County through someone else's eyes.

description:
Welcome… to Discover the Terror!
Your ghoulish host, Maximilian Schmidt and Zombaby co-host, Herbert, will lead you hand-in-hand through the dark corridors of hell, exploring some of horror's most intriguing voices, both rising talents and established icons.
But horror isn't just fiction. It's real. In addition to artists and filmmakers, Maximilian speaks with individuals immersed in the worlds of the supernatural, the paranormal, and the uncanny. Psychics, explorers, survivors… anyone with a story soaked in terror is welcome in Maximilian's chair.
This show exists to unpack and digest the subjects we're too afraid to face. To ask: Why is humankind so obsessed with horror, and yet so repelled by it?
Horror is the most universal genre. And fear is the most universal feeling. These are two abstract, unending forces that Maximilian and his guests dive into, headfirst, in every episode.
With Discover the Terror, the unknown becomes known… or at least, a little less unknowable. Maximilian Schmidt is a devoted student of horror, a writer and director unafraid to confront the most complex, unsettling aspects of human nature and the physical body. His mission: to tell and uncover honest stories that focus on outsiders, "freaks," and the beautifully dark corners of humanity.

author: First Not Only Network
description:
Growth doesn't happen in a straight line. It happens in seasons like a garden if you will. There's the season where everything's dormant, and it feels like nothing is happening at all. There's the season where you're all root, no bloom — doing the invisible work nobody claps for. And then, if you tended it right, there's the season where you're finally in full bloom. 
This show is for all three. Every episode, we're sitting down with people who've done the growing — in public, in private, in boardrooms, in the middle of a total replant or pivot. 
We're not just here for the bloom though. We want the whole root system: the failure that fed the soil, the pivot nobody saw coming, the season they almost gave up on the garden entirely. Because if you've ever been the first — or the only one — you already know something about growing in conditions you weren't necessarily planted for. You know that growth isn't optional. It's how you survive. And eventually, it's how you thrive. 
So consider this your garden. A place you come back to, season after season, to see what's actually possible when something gets planted, tended, and given time. 
I'm Janis Middleton, and this is The First, Not Only Network Podcast.

title: ALL in
author: Graeme Codrington
description:
A podcast about Christians, the Church, the Bible, our Faith and what we need to do to affirm and include the LGTBQI community - especially those who are seeking Jesus and who want to be involved in the Church.

We believe the Bible is God's word - through the ages and for today. We should study it, understand it and apply it to our lives. 

Hosted by Graeme Codrington, with a masters degree in theology, who was ordained in the Baptist Union of South Africa many years ago, yet changed his conservative view that the LGBTQI community are in deed sinners in need of salvation. After 15 years of studying the scriptures, investigating this topic, speaking with people and engaging with this community, we believe that God made some people gay and that we should accept and embrace the LGTBQI community as God's creations, loved by Him for who they are, not for who they are meant to be. 

In our podcast episodes

- We'll take you through the evidence found in Scripture, and seen through church history and traditions.

- We'll ask what this means for churches - what it looks like for churches to affirm the LGBTQI community, and what we should be saying and doing. Together with what this community should be hearing.

- We'll be sharing some of the stories LGBTQI Christians who love Jesus, and who love the church - even though the church has, in the most part, been so hateful to them. These are people who are desperately seeking Jesus and we must hear their stories. 

- We'll also share some of the stories of people who love Jesus, but hate the church - so that we can hear what the church should be doing. And then, of course, there are those stories of people who used to love Jesus but who know hate Jesus and the Church, because of what the church has done. We need to hear those stories too.

Every week, we take one story from football's hidden history and tell it properly: the cartels that bought Colombia's clubs, the dictator who threatened his own World Cup squad, the political prisoners who built a football association inside apartheid's most notorious jail, the man who spent twenty years as a professional footballer without really playing.


These are stories where football isn't just the backdrop. It's where power, crime, politics, faith and identity collide, and where the game itself changes what happens next. Each episode goes back into the history that shaped the story, the people caught up in it, and the side stories that most accounts leave out.


Some episodes are dark. Some are absurd. All of them are true.

Each episode explores the things that make life interesting: pop culture, cinema, television, motherhood, domestic life, food, gardening, seasonal living, beauty, nostalgia and the strange little obsessions that get us through the week.

title: And All the Animals
author: Useful Monsters
description:
And All the Animals is a walk through the whole Bible — start to finish, in order, one story at a time.

There are two voices. A narrator tells the story. A raven supplies the facts: what a cubit works out to, how big Nineveh actually was, which museum the tablet is sitting in. The raven was, by its own account, present for some of this, and has not entirely gotten over how that turned out.

The stories are told straight, which means the people in them come off exactly as badly as the text says they do. Jacob is a con man. Noah gets off the boat and plants a vineyard. The prophet in episode one would rather die than watch his enemies be forgiven. The Bible's own narrator is unsparing about all of it — we just say it out loud.

Where a passage has been read two ways for a thousand years, we say so, lay both out as well as we can, and leave it with you. Where the archaeology is contested, you get the dates, the findspots, and an honest shrug. Episodes end on a question rather than a moral.

description:
The History of the English Language Podcast, hosted by Josh Linsk, explores how English developed from its earliest roots into one of the world’s most widely spoken languages. Each episode traces the people, migrations, invasions, cultures, technologies, and historical events that shaped English vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, spelling, and everyday speech.

The podcast follows the language through Old English, the Anglo-Saxon period, Viking influence, the Norman Conquest, Middle English, the Great Vowel Shift, Early Modern English, Shakespeare, the printing press, colonial expansion, American English, and the rise of English as a global language. Along the way, it examines where words came from, why meanings changed, how accents developed, and how English absorbed influences from Latin, French, Norse, Greek, and many other languages.

Eventually, the crimes would become connected to one unknown offender.
But his identity remained a mystery.
Then, in 2018, investigators used a relatively new forensic technique — investigative genetic genealogy — to identify a suspect who had remained hidden in plain sight for decades.
His name was Joseph James DeAngelo.
In this episode of The Global Casebook, we follow the investigation from its earliest crimes through the decades-long search, the breakthrough in genetic genealogy, DeAngelo's arrest, his guilty plea and the final chapter of one of America's most notorious cold cases.

This second season of Between Borders focuses on care, which has become a central theme in migration research and solidarity work, not least since the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Attitudes
author: Kitty Sunnucks
description:
ATTITUDES is the podcast about what Britain really thinks.


Hosted by Mark Easton, Senior Fellow at The National Centre for Social Research (NatCen) and former BBC Home Editor, each episode takes a headline finding from some of the UK's most robust social research and explores what it reveals about the way we think, live and see the world. From artificial intelligence to taxation, cannabis to nuclear energy, Mark and expert guests dig beneath the headlines to uncover what evidence tells us about public attitudes over time.


At a time when public debate is often shaped by assumptions, ATTITUDES brings evidence to the conversation. Drawing on more than 40 years of research from NatCen, the UK's largest independent social research organisation, the series reveals how public attitudes are changing and challenges what we think we know about Britain.


Join us as we go beyond the numbers and discover what Britain really thinks.

Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

title: For Those Who Listen
author: The Voice
description:
Hosted by The Voice, 
For Those Who Listen is a space where we observe how we respond. 
it's no small secret 
how explosive we can be,
especially to those 
we believe don't belong.
reactions on reactions 
dividing us into factions,
dressed in justification and pride, 
all in the name of being right.
while reactions run rampant in the hearts of millions everyday, 
For Those Who Listen exists 
as the calm collected antithesis. 
if the world is truly so divided,
how does one turn the tide?
by honoring the arts,
the mind & observing what's inside.
in knowing… we still...
have time.
